item.title: [0day-rubbish] Dataedo Portal 26.2.8 with Dataedo Agent 26.2.8 unrestricted scheduler job-type deserialization to Agent-host command execution (8.1)
item.description:
Dataedo Portal 26.2.8 has a static AES key baked into its shipped DLL that exposes repo credentials, chaining into unrestricted Hangfire deserialization on the Agent host for OS command execution, scored CVSS 8.1 High with no patch and no CVE yet assigned.
Key findings:
- The chain starts at GET /api/repository/connection-string, which returns the repository DB credential encrypted with SimpleAES: AES-256-CBC with a 32-byte key and 16-byte IV hardcoded as byte-array literals in the shipped Dataedo.Settings.dll, byte-identical across every build and referenced from 19 assemblies. The same static pair is published in the proof-of-concept. In the tested deployment the recovered login was sa, a sysadmin-level principal over the database that also holds the Hangfire scheduler storage in the [Scheduler] schema. No gadget chain is required: the invocation document names System.Diagnostics.Process/Start directly, with cmd.exe and the payload as arguments, inserted as two rows into [Scheduler].Job and [Scheduler].JobQueue.
- The Agent side registers no ITypeResolver restriction and no invocation allowlist with either its default or priority Hangfire queue. FilterInitializer calls GlobalJobFilters.Clear() and adds four filters, none of which constrains execution type at runtime: the two IClientFilter implementations return early unless the type implements ISchedulerTaskExecutor, the IApplyStateFilter reacts only to DeletedState transitions, and AutomaticRetry is set to Attempts=0. After Clear() nothing in the execution path inspects the invocation type, declaring type, method name, or arguments. Execution was observed at nt authority\system when the Agent ran as a SYSTEM-privileged service, and at the local administrator account when launched interactively. The report is explicit that the SYSTEM outcome reflects the test harness service configuration, not a confirmed universal default.
- Exploitation requires PR:H (role action 11 or above on the Portal), a network path to the repository listener, and at least one Agent attached to that repository. The CVSS 3.1 vector is AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H = 8.1. Scope is Changed because the impacted component is a separately installed process on a separate host reached only through the repository database. A conditional vector of 9.1 applies where an attached Agent and reachable listener are known, which is the ordinary topology for any deployment using scheduling features.
- The adjacent disclosure group (unscored, no patch) adds: 18 ungated routes on RepositoryController enabling anonymous repository registration during any unconfigured window; anonymous rewrite of configuration[WEB_CATALOG_URL] via POST /api/repository/connect-and-upgrade on a healthy instance, converting the portal into a credential-phishing surface; outbound TDS to attacker-named hosts through available-databases (NetNTLMv2 exposure on Windows); SSRF through /api/text-editor/link reaching internal services and cloud instance metadata (HTTP 200 observed); wildcard CORS (SetIsOriginAllowed(_ => true) with AllowCredentials and SameSite=None) covering the entire cookie-authenticated /api/* surface; and a default JWT signing key (shipped GUID, ValidateIssuer=false, ValidateAudience=false) affecting container and non-wizard deployments.
- Detection signals the report names: an InvocationData value in [Scheduler].Job whose Type field names anything outside the vendor's scheduler job namespace, especially System.Diagnostics.Process; a State.Result of "Can not serialize the return value" on a completed job; PerformanceDuration in the low single-digit milliseconds for a non-vendor job type; shell binaries in the Arguments column; a JobQueue row whose FetchedAt is never populated (preparation with no consumer); unexpected child processes of the Agent service on the Agent host; and POST traffic to repository registration and connect-and-upgrade routes from unauthenticated clients, or a change in configuration[WEB_CATALOG_URL] or appsettings.json.
Practitioner takeaway: No patch exists and no CVE has been assigned. Until one arrives, restrict network access to the repository listener to Portal and Agent hosts only, enable database auditing on [Scheduler].Job and [Scheduler].JobQueue inserts and alert on the Type and State.Result signals above, treat any principal with [Scheduler] write access as holding command execution on every attached Agent host, complete first-run repository configuration immediately after install, rotate the repository credential and treat every prior copy as exposed (any repo-management principal can recover it on demand), inventory Dataedo-Web-backup-*.zip artifacts as credential material, strip reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with credentials at the reverse proxy, and rotate the JWT signing key on any deployment that did not pass through the installer's API-configuration wizard. Treat the Agent host as a crown-jewel system for the duration.

In the tested deployment the recovered login was sa, a sysadmin-level principal over the database that also holds the Hangfire scheduler storage in the [Scheduler] schema. No gadget chain is required: the invocation document names System.Diagnostics.Process/Start directly, with cmd.exe and the payload as arguments, inserted as two rows into [Scheduler].Job and [Scheduler].JobQueue.

- The Agent side registers no ITypeResolver restriction and no invocation allowlist with either its default or priority Hangfire queue. FilterInitializer calls GlobalJobFilters.Clear() and adds four filters, none of which constrains execution type at runtime: the two IClientFilter implementations return early unless the type implements ISchedulerTaskExecutor, the IApplyStateFilter reacts only to DeletedState transitions, and AutomaticRetry is set to Attempts=0. After Clear() nothing in the execution path inspects the invocation type, declaring type, method name, or arguments. Execution was observed at nt authority\system when the Agent ran as a SYSTEM-privileged service, and at the local administrator account when launched interactively. The report is explicit that the SYSTEM outcome reflects the test harness service configuration, not a confirmed universal default.

- Exploitation requires PR:H (role action 11 or above on the Portal), a network path to the repository listener, and at least one Agent attached to that repository. The CVSS 3.1 vector is AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H = 8.1. Scope is Changed because the impacted component is a separately installed process on a separate host reached only through the repository database. A conditional vector of 9.1 applies where an attached Agent and reachable listener are known, which is the ordinary topology for any deployment using scheduling features.

- The adjacent disclosure group (unscored, no patch) adds: 18 ungated routes on RepositoryController enabling anonymous repository registration during any unconfigured window; anonymous rewrite of configuration[WEB_CATALOG_URL] via POST /api/repository/connect-and-upgrade on a healthy instance, converting the portal into a credential-phishing surface; outbound TDS to attacker-named hosts through available-databases (NetNTLMv2 exposure on Windows); SSRF through /api/text-editor/link reaching internal services and cloud instance metadata (HTTP 200 observed); wildcard CORS (SetIsOriginAllowed(_ => true) with AllowCredentials and SameSite=None) covering the entire cookie-authenticated /api/* surface; and a default JWT signing key (shipped GUID, ValidateIssuer=false, ValidateAudience=false) affecting container and non-wizard deployments.

- Detection signals the report names: an InvocationData value in [Scheduler].Job whose Type field names anything outside the vendor's scheduler job namespace, especially System.Diagnostics.Process; a State.Result of "Can not serialize the return value" on a completed job; PerformanceDuration in the low single-digit milliseconds for a non-vendor job type; shell binaries in the Arguments column; a JobQueue row whose FetchedAt is never populated (preparation with no consumer); unexpected child processes of the Agent service on the Agent host; and POST traffic to repository registration and connect-and-upgrade routes from unauthenticated clients, or a change in configuration[WEB_CATALOG_URL] or appsettings.json.

Practitioner takeaway: No patch exists and no CVE has been assigned. Until one arrives, restrict network access to the repository listener to Portal and Agent hosts only, enable database auditing on [Scheduler].Job and [Scheduler].JobQueue inserts and alert on the Type and State.Result signals above, treat any principal with [Scheduler] write access as holding command execution on every attached Agent host, complete first-run repository configuration immediately after install, rotate the repository credential and treat every prior copy as exposed (any repo-management principal can recover it on demand), inventory Dataedo-Web-backup-*.zip artifacts as credential material, strip reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with credentials at the reverse proxy, and rotate the JWT signing key on any deployment that did not pass through the installer's API-configuration wizard. Treat the Agent host as a crown-jewel system for the duration.

item.title: The Threat of AI-Driven Autonomous Penetration Testing, as Examined by ARTEX
item.description:
AI-driven autonomous penetration testing is no longer theoretical. AhnLab ASEC tracked an internet-exposed ARTEX instance and found operational attack artifacts on associated hosts, confirming the tool is being used beyond proof-of-concept.
- AhnLab identified 600 public IPs hosting ARTEX instances, with 90.2% concentrated across the US 🇺🇸, China 🇨🇳, Hong Kong, and Singapore 🇸🇬. As of October 14, 2026, approximately 900 IPs associated with the ARTEX operating system were publicly accessible. Two of those 600 IPs were directly tied to operational attack directories, and investigators recovered 51 files across those two open directories, including ws[.]sh (a script written to send commands to an ASPX web shell), pivot_relay.ps1 (configured to relay external connections to internal RDP), extract_hprof.py (written to extract credentials from JVM heap dumps), P.class (designed to download and execute a Linux implant), and LocaleMgr.exe (containing strings indicating command execution, file manipulation, and tunneling). Scan results in the second directory listed 85 active systems in a Kubernetes Pod network and 8 in a separate internal network. The IOC table in the report contains 2 IPs (134.122.137[.]132 and 204.194.51[.]54) and 18 MD5 hashes tied to these directories.
- ARTEX operates through three agent roles: Goals (organizes objectives and test scope), Planner (reviews gathered information and determines next steps), and Worker (executes tools and records verified results). Asset context is stored in a PostgreSQL-backed Asset Graph and Exploration Graph, allowing the system to reason across tasks without repeating prior reconnaissance. On the target side, logs record the tool requests and process behavior, not any agent name, which limits visibility into the AI layer driving the attack.
- In two controlled reproduction tests, ARTEX received only a brief plaintext objective with no vulnerability details, no tool guidance, and no human intervention mid-run. Against a web server with a file upload vulnerability, it located the upload path, deployed a web shell, and executed a program on a Windows 11 host. Against an Apache ActiveMQ 5.15.15 instance, it autonomously identified CVE-2023-46604 on TCP port 61616, modified XML to establish a PowerShell shell, and then pivoted to achieve remote command execution on four internal hosts following initial access to the boundary server BEACHHEAD01. External tools including nmap, nxc, and Impacket were selected and invoked without user instruction.
- User-Agent detection is unreliable as a primary control. ARTEX recorded "artex-selfupdate" for GitHub update checks, "norma/0.4" for web page access, and "curl/VERSION" for file uploads during testing. The source code specifies "artex-enrich/1.0" and "Mozilla/5.0 (Spa-api-recon)" variants exist but were not active in the analyzed version. Non-HTTP communications (SMB, OpenWire on port 61616, RDP relay) leave no User-Agent trace at all, and threat actors can trivially modify or suppress these values.
DFIR takeaway: Do not anchor your hunt to User-Agent strings. The real signal is behavioral sequencing across log sources. Look for the chain: external service scan or probe, followed by file write or web shell creation on a web-accessible path, followed by a new process spawned from a web server process, followed by outbound SMB or RDP from that host to internal segments. Correlate web access logs, firewall connection logs, and endpoint process execution logs together. For the ActiveMQ angle specifically, the report ties exploitation of CVE-2023-46604 to TCP port 61616 and XML modification as the mechanism for shell establishment, so watch for unexpected child processes under ActiveMQ service processes and PowerShell spawning in that context. The full IOC table with 2 IPs and 18 MD5 hashes is in the report.

item.title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
item.description:
CVE-2026-74580 "Vghost": a Linux kernel vhost flaw gives any local user reliable kernel read/write and root across nearly a decade of kernels, with a second path that lets a VM escape to the host's QEMU process.
Key findings:
- The bug lives in Linux's vhost subsystem, reachable by opening /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock. A stale translation cache, introduced across two separate commits (a 2017 cache addition in Linux 4.11 and a 2020 check relocation in Linux 5.9), lets VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR and VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM reconfigure a live ring's addresses without invalidating that cache. Subsequent copies use the old, unchecked mapping, producing an out-of-bounds kernel read and write. The local-privilege-escalation chain is deterministic, needs no heap grooming and no timing luck, bypasses KASLR, and reaches root. No public exploitation has been observed.
- The guest-to-host escape is narrower but severe. It requires a virtio device behind a virtual IOMMU with iommu_platform enabled and vhost running in device-IOTLB mode. An untrusted guest triggers the same stale-cache path, causing the host kernel to write out of bounds into the host's QEMU process. From there, an attacker can overwrite a function pointer in QEMU and redirect host execution, or crash the hypervisor. The kernel[.]org CVE team scores this 8.8 with scope marked "changed" because the write crosses the guest-to-host boundary. Red Hat scores it 7.3, Amazon 7.8, Oracle 7.3.
- Affected range is Linux 4.11 through 7.2-rc4. Tencent confirmed the full local-to-root chain on Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 9.8, Amazon Linux 2023, Microsoft Azure Linux 3.0, and Oracle Linux 10.2. On Ubuntu, the device node is group-restricted to kvm, so the entry point is a kvm group member. On the other four images, /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock were world-readable at mode 0666, meaning any local user was in scope. The fix is commit de845981da67, which clears the cache on every ring reconfiguration. First fixed stable versions range from 5.10.265 through 7.1.9 across seven maintained branches. Red Hat, Amazon, and Oracle have shipped fixes; Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 fixes were still in progress as of October 13.
- The flaw was found with help from Corvus AI, a multi-agent kernel vulnerability research pipeline Tencent Zhuque Lab built in-house. The upstream commit credits it with an Assisted-by line. This is the same team and toolchain that disclosed an 18-year-old SCTP kernel flaw in August 2026, also reaching root and container escape. This is machine-assisted research, not an autonomous attack.
Practitioner takeaway: check your vhost device node permissions before a patch lands. Run "stat /dev/vhost-net /dev/vhost-vsock" on every Linux host and container host in your environment. If either shows mode 0666, remove world access and restrict the owning group to trusted virtualization services immediately. Treat kvm or equivalent group membership as a sensitive privilege while the vulnerable kernel runs. For the guest-to-host path, no workaround exists: the patched kernel is the only remedy, so prioritize hypervisor hosts, cloud-adjacent Linux images, and any multi-tenant environment where local access is broadly granted. The report includes working proof-of-concept demos for both attack chains.
